extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent office officials (receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, International Bureau)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory/formal requirements for preparing and filing PCT (international) patent applications, including claims, drawings, abstract, language/translation, physical format, unity, biological-material references, and sequence listings. Intended to ensure compliance with PCT Rules and smooth processing by Offices and Authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependent claims: format and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim which refers to more than one other claim (“multiple dependent claim”) shall refer to such claims in the alternative only. Multiple dependent claims shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the national law of the national Office acting as ISA does not allow multiple dependent claims to be drafted in a manner different from that provided, failure to use that manner may result in an indication under Article 17(2)(b) in the international search report. Failure to use the said manner shall have no effect in a designated State if the manner actually used satisfies the national law of that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent-claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dependent claim shall be construed as including all the limitations contained in the claim to which it refers or, if the dependent claim is a multiple dependent claim, all the limitations contained in the particular claim in relation to which it is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims add the limitations of the claims they refer to; multiple-dependent claims incorporate the limitations of the particular claim being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All dependent claims referring back to a single previous claim, and all dependent claims referring back to several previous claims, shall be grouped together to the extent and in the most practical way possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange dependent claims logically and practically so related dependent claims appear together for clarity and processing efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model treatment by designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: Any designated State in which the grant of a utility model is sought on the basis of an international application may, instead of Rules 6.1 to 6.4, apply its national law concerning utility models once processing in that State has started, provided the applicant is allowed at least two months from the expiration of the time limit applicable under Article 22 to adapt the application to national requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated States can apply national utility-model regimes; applicants must be given at least two months after the Article 22 time limit to make required adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow sheets and diagrams considered drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow sheets and diagrams are considered drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat flow charts and process diagrams as drawings for the purposes of the drawing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for filing drawings or additional drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 7(2)(ii) shall be reasonable under the circumstances of the case and shall, in no case, be shorter than two months from the date of the written invitation requiring the filing of drawings or additional drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices/Authorities must allow a reasonable period but not less than two months after invitation to submit drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall consist of a summary of the disclosure as contained in the description, the claims, and any drawings; the summary shall indicate the technical field, allow clear understanding of the technical problem, the gist of the solution through the invention, and the principal use or uses of the invention. Where applicable, include the chemical formula which best characterizes the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract must summarize disclosure across description/claims/drawings and highlight field, problem, solution gist, principal uses; include representative chemical formula if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be as concise as the disclosure permits (preferably 50 to 150 words if it is in English or when translated into English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for 50–150 words in English; be as concise as possible while conveying the necessary scanning information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: prohibited content
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall not contain statements on the alleged merits or value of the claimed invention or on its speculative application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use promotional or speculative language in the abstract; keep it factual and technical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: reference signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each main technical feature mentioned in the abstract and illustrated by a drawing shall be followed by a reference sign, placed between parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to drawing-illustrated features in the abstract, include the drawing reference sign in parentheses for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure selection for abstract publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant fails to indicate a figure for the abstract, or if the ISA finds a different figure(s) better characterizes the invention, the ISA may indicate the figure(s) to accompany the abstract when published. If the ISA finds none useful, the abstract shall be published without any figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA may select the figure(s) that best characterize the invention for publication or determine no figure is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract drafting guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be so drafted that it can efficiently serve as a scanning tool for purposes of searching in the particular art, especially by assisting the scientist, engineer or researcher in formulating an opinion on whether there is a need for consulting the international application itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write abstracts to enable quick relevance assessment by specialists; ensure it helps decide whether to read the full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited expressions and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall not contain: (i) expressions or drawings contrary to morality; (ii) expressions or drawings contrary to public order; (iii) statements disparaging the products or processes of any particular person other than the applicant, or the merits or validity of applications or patents of any such person (mere comparisons with the prior art shall not be considered disparaging per se); (iv) any statement or other matter obviously irrelevant or unnecessary under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid immoral, public-order-contrary, disparaging or irrelevant content; comparisons with prior art are acceptable if not disparaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation of lack of compliance with expression rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office, the ISA, the Authority for supplementary search and the International Bureau may note lack of compliance with Rule 9.1 and may suggest to the applicant that he voluntarily correct his international application accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices/Authorities may flag non-compliant wording/drawings and suggest voluntary corrections; they shall be informed if applicant follows suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and temperature expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Units of weights and measures shall be expressed in terms of the metric system, or also expressed in such terms if first expressed in a different system. Temperatures shall be expressed in degrees Celsius, or also expressed in degrees Celsius if first expressed differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer metric units and Celsius; if other systems used, also include metric/Celsius equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies to file
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application and each of the documents referred to in the checklist shall be filed in one copy, subject to receiving Office provisions; any receiving Office may require two or three copies (except fee receipt), in which case it must verify identity of the extra copies with the record copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is single copy; check receiving Office local requirements for 2–3 copies and identity verification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct reproduction and consistency of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: All elements of the international application (request, description, claims, drawings, abstract) shall be so presented as to admit of direct reproduction by photography, electrostatic processes, photo offset, and microfilming, in any number of copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format documents to be reproducible by common reprographic techniques; avoid features that impede reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet condition and single-sided use
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets shall be free from creases and cracks; they shall not be folded. Only one side of each sheet shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clean, uncreased, unfolded sheets and print/write on one side only to ensure reproduction quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Rules 11.10(d) and 11.13(j), each sheet shall be used in an upright position (short sides at top and bottom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present sheets upright unless explicitly permitted otherwise (e.g., sideways tables/figures per rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material quality for application sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: All elements shall be on paper which shall be flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-quality paper suitable for reproduction and archival storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and signs consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminology and the signs shall be consistent throughout the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent terms and reference signs across description, claims, and drawings to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each element on a new sheet; connection of sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each element (request, description, claims, drawings, abstract) shall commence on a new sheet. All sheets shall be so connected that they can be easily turned when consulted, and easily separated and joined again if separated for reproduction purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start each major part on its own sheet and bind/arrange sheets for easy consultation and reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of sheets (A4) and acceptance of other sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of the sheets shall be A4 (29.7 cm x 21 cm). However, any receiving Office may accept other sizes provided the record copy and, if required, the search copy, shall be of A4 size when transmitted to the International Bureau and ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer A4; if another size accepted locally, ensure record/search copies are A4 for transmission purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins: minimum and recommended maximum
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum margins for sheets containing description, claims, and abstract: top 2 cm; left 2.5 cm; right 2 cm; bottom 2 cm. Recommended maximums: top 4 cm; left 4 cm; right 3 cm; bottom 3 cm. For drawings, usable surface shall not exceed 26.2 x 17.0 cm and minimum margins (drawings): top 2.5 cm; left 2.5 cm; right 1.5 cm; bottom 1 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe margin minima to permit reproduction; recommended maxima help with readability. Margins apply to A4 sheets; even if other sizes used, A4 copies must leave prescribed margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins must be blank except applicant file reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The margins of the international application, when submitted, must be completely blank. The top margin may contain in the left‑hand corner an indication of the applicant's file reference, provided it appears within 1.5 cm from the top; number of characters limited by Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep margins free of content except permitted applicant file reference in top-left, within specified space and character limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets and lines
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets shall be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, centered at top or bottom (not in the margin). It is strongly recommended to number every fifth line of each sheet of the description and of each sheet of claims; the numbers should appear in the right half of the left margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number sheets consecutively; line-numbering every fifth line aids citation and examination—place line numbers per recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing/typing of text matter: format and size
rubrics_metrics.description: The request, description, claims and the abstract shall be typed or printed. Only graphic symbols/formulae and certain characters in Chinese/Japanese may be handwritten when necessary. Typing shall be 1½‑spaced. All text matter shall be in characters the capital letters of which are not less than 0.28 cm high and in a dark, indelible color; request text may use characters with capital letters not less than 0.21 cm high. Paragraphs (c) and (d) do not apply to Chinese or Japanese texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, legible typed/printed text at minimum size; maintain 1.5 line spacing; check special provisions for request and Asian scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No drawings in request, description, claims, abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The request, the description, the claims and the abstract shall not contain drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep graphical content (drawings) separate; include only minimal indispensable words in drawings per Rule 11.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulae and tables in text: placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Description, claims and abstract may contain chemical or mathematical formulae. Description and abstract may contain tables; any claim may contain tables only if the subject matter of the claim makes the use of tables desirable. Tables and chemical/mathematical formulae may be placed sideways if they cannot be presented satisfactorily upright; when sideways, tops of tables/formulae must be at the left side of the sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sideways placement only when necessary, orient them as specified to ensure correct reproduction and reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words in drawings: limitation and placement for translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall not contain text matter, except a single word or words when absolutely indispensable (e.g., 'water', 'steam', 'open', 'closed', 'section on AB', or short catchwords in circuits or flow diagrams). Any words used shall be so placed that, if translated, they may be pasted over without interfering with drawing lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep textual content in drawings to an absolute minimum and place it to permit straightforward translation overlays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations, erasures and overwritings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sheet shall be reasonably free from erasures and shall be free from alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Non-compliance with this Rule may be authorized if the authenticity of the content is not in question and the requirements for good reproduction are not in jeopardy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid corrections on submitted sheets; where unavoidable, ensure authenticity and reproduction quality are maintained and seek authorization if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing execution standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be executed in durable, black, sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined lines and strokes without colorings. Cross-sections indicated by oblique hatching which should not impede reading of reference signs. Scale and distinctness such that a photographic reproduction with linear reduction to two-thirds enables all details to be distinguished. Lines ordinarily drawn with drafting instruments. Each element of a figure shall be in proper proportion (unless different proportion indispensable). Height of numbers and letters not less than 0.32 cm; Latin and, where customary, Greek alphabets used. Same sheet may contain several figures; where figures on several sheets form a complete figure, they must be arranged to assemble without concealing parts. Figures arranged without wasting space and preferably upright. Figures numbered in Arabic numerals consecutively and independently of sheet numbering. Reference signs not mentioned in the description shall not appear in drawings and vice versa; same features denoted by same signs throughout; if many reference signs, attach separate list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow detailed graphic standards to ensure clarity at reductions, consistent reference signs, legible lettering, and orderly figure arrangement; provide a reference-sign list if numerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules applied to later-submitted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 10 and 11.1 to 11.13 also apply to any document (for example, replacement sheets, amended claims, translations) submitted after the filing of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure replacement/amended documents and later submissions also comply with physical and formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language acceptance for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall be filed in any language which the receiving Office accepts for that purpose. Each receiving Office shall accept at least one language that is both: (i) a language accepted by the ISA (or at least one of the ISAs competent for that receiving Office), and (ii) a language of publication. Notwithstanding paragraph (a), the request shall be filed in any language of publication which the receiving Office accepts for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File in a language accepted by the receiving Office; ensure at least one accepted language meets ISA/publication acceptance requirements; file request in an accepted publication language if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of sequence-listing and language-dependent free text
rubrics_metrics.description: Any language-dependent free text contained in the sequence listing part of the description shall be filed in a language which the receiving Office accepts for that purpose. Elements/parts furnished under certain rules must be in the language of the international application as filed or, where a translation is required, in both languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Administrative Instructions for sequence listings and ensure language-dependent text is filed in acceptable languages; some furnished elements may need dual-language submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of amendments and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment of the international application shall, subject to certain rules, be in the language in which the application is filed. Rectifications of obvious mistakes and corrections under specified rules shall generally be in the language filed, with specific exceptions where translations of the application or request are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit amendments/corrections in the application's filing language unless specific rules require otherwise; follow exceptions when translations are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation for international search (12.3): when required and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the filing language is not accepted by the ISA to carry out the international search, the applicant shall, within one month from receipt by the receiving Office, furnish a translation into a language accepted by that Authority and a language of publication and accepted by the receiving Office (unless filed in a language of publication). If translation not furnished, the receiving Office shall invite the applicant to furnish it; failure within time limits may lead to withdrawal of the international application. Furnishing a translation late may incur a late furnishing fee (25% of international filing fee) and other time-limit consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required search translations promptly (one month) into acceptable language(s); heed invitations and pay late-furnishing fees if late; missing translations can lead to withdrawal unless furnished before declared withdrawal or before certain time thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation for international publication (12.4): when required and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the filing language is not a language of publication and no translation is required under Rule 12.3, the applicant shall, within 14 months from the priority date, furnish a translation into any language of publication which the receiving Office accepts. If not furnished, the receiving Office shall invite the applicant and may require a late furnishing fee; failure to comply within the extended time limit may lead to declaration of withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide publication translations by 14 months from priority date (or respond to invitations) to avoid withdrawal; late furnishing may require a fee and has specific time-bound consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-furnishing fee for translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The furnishing of a translation after the expiration of the time limit may be subjected by the receiving Office to payment, for its own benefit, of a late furnishing fee equal to 25% of the international filing fee referred to in item 1 of the Schedule of Fees, not taking into account any fee for each sheet in excess of 30 sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late translations are possible in some circumstances but will usually incur a 25% late-furnishing fee; check receiving Office practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to furnish required translation (withdrawal)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does not furnish a required translation and pay any late-furnishing fee within the applicable invited time limit, the receiving Office shall consider the international application withdrawn and so declare, subject to specified exceptions where translations/payments are received before particular time thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely translations/payment are critical; missing them risks formal withdrawal of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing documents related to earlier searches (Rule 12bis.1 & .2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant requests the ISA to take into account earlier search results (Rule 4.12), the applicant shall submit, with the international application, a copy of results of the earlier search in whatever form they are presented. The ISA may invite the applicant to furnish copies or translations of earlier applications, search results, or cited documents within a reasonable time. If copies/translations are available to Office/ISA (e.g., digital library), submission may not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on earlier searches, provide copies/translations proactively or indicate availability in digital resources; respond to ISA invitations within reasonable time to facilitate taking earlier searches into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept (‘requirement of unity of invention’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must satisfy unity: either a single invention or several linked by a single general inventive concept to avoid lack-of-unity objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: When unity is fulfilled (special technical features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is fulfilled only when there is a technical relationship among the claimed inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. ‘Special technical features’ means those technical features that define a contribution which each claimed invention, considered as a whole, makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess unity by identifying shared special technical features that contribute over prior art; group inventions claiming the same contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unity independent of manner of claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether a group of inventions is so linked as to form a single general inventive concept shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity assessment focuses on technical relationship, not claim drafting strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims: reasonable number allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Rule 13.1, it shall be permitted to include in the same international application a reasonable number of dependent claims, claiming specific forms of the invention claimed in an independent claim, even where the features of any dependent claim could be considered as constituting in themselves an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include a reasonable number of dependent claims to cover specific embodiments; check national limits in designated States.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to deposited biological material: required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to deposited biological material shall indicate: (i) the name and address of the depositary institution; (ii) the date of deposit; (iii) the accession number given by that institution; and (iv) any additional matter of which the International Bureau has been notified and published in the Gazette at least two months before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full deposit details to satisfy national requirements; check Gazette notices for any extra required particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to include biological-deposit reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to include a reference to deposited biological material or failure to include required indications in a reference shall have no consequence in any designated State whose national law does not require such reference or such indication in a national application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact depends on each designated State’s national law; include references to be safe, especially where national law requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for furnishing biological-material indications
rubrics_metrics.description: If any required indication for a reference to deposited biological material is not included in the application as filed but is furnished to the International Bureau within 16 months from the priority date, the indication shall be considered by any designated Office to have been furnished in time. Indications furnished after 16 months may be considered furnished on the last day of that time limit if received before technical preparations for publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide missing deposit information by 16 months from priority date to be treated as timely; designated Offices may require earlier furnishing per national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of biological samples
rubrics_metrics.description: No furnishing of samples of the deposited biological material to which a reference is made shall, except with authorization of the applicant, take place before the expiration of the applicable time limits after which national processing may start. However, if the applicant performs acts under Articles 22 or 39 after international publication but before expiration of those time limits, furnishing may take place once those acts are performed. Notwithstanding the previous provision, furnishing may take place under national law when international publication has the effects of compulsory national publication of an unexamined national application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biological samples are generally withheld until national processing starts or applicant authorizes; be aware of exceptions if applicant acts under certain Articles or national law provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: National notification/publication of biological-deposit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any national Office may notify the International Bureau of national-law requirements for additional particulars to be included in references to deposited biological material or of time requirements earlier than 16 months. Each national Office shall notify the International Bureau of depositary institutions permitted under its national law. The International Bureau shall promptly publish such notifications in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor PCT Gazette and national notifications for state-specific deposit requirements and accepted depositary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings: furnishing for international search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences that, pursuant to the Administrative Instructions, are required to be included in a sequence listing, the ISA may invite the applicant to furnish a sequence listing complying with the standard provided for in the Administrative Instructions, unless such listing is already available to it in a form, language and manner acceptable to it, and to pay any applicable late-furnishing fee within a time limit fixed in the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sequence listings in the required standard and language when invited by the ISA; late furnishing may incur fees—consult Administrative Instructions for format standards.
